chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: "O Abd al-Malik, why do I not see you going out to these places that the people of your country go to?"
I said: "And where?" He said: "Jeddah, Abbadan, al-Masissah, and Qazvin."
I said: "Awaiting your command and following your example." He said: "Yes, by Allah, if it were good, they would have preceded us to it."
I said: "Indeed, the Zaydiyyah say that there is no difference between us and Ja'far except that he does not consider Jihad (to be obligatory)."
He said: "I do not consider it (obligatory), by Allah, I do consider it, but I dislike that I should make my knowledge known to their ignorance."

key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّةَ: The Zaydiyyah, a Shia sect following Zayd ibn Ali
key_terms.الْجِهَادَ: Jihad, striving in the path of God

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq avoid the Zaydiyyah gatherings despite agreeing on Jihad?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that his absence from Zaydi gatherings in Jeddah and Qazvin was not due to a disagreement on the obligation of Jihad, but rather a strategic choice to avoid premature association with their 'ignorance' (jahlihim). This reflects the Shia scholarly principle of distinguishing between the core tenet of Jihad and the specific political or theological context of the Zaydi movement, ensuring that the Imam's authority and knowledge were not conflated with their specific claims.
